headline: Workday has launched AI agents that work on their own in the background, a platform that lets other AI tools use its software, and a hiring agent in early access.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 1: the announcements were made at Workday Rising from 13 Oct 2026, before the 16 Oct window, our 14 Oct edition already carried the conference, and the benefit claims are Workday's own.
importance_line: Employees whose HR, finance and IT requests pass through Workday will deal with agents that act without being asked, and companies get tools for controlling them, but the productivity claims are Workday's own and the agents' real-world error rates are not reported.
summary: iTWire and InformationWeek report from Workday Rising in Las Vegas (keynote 13 Oct 2026) that Workday, a maker of HR and finance software, unveiled "autopilot" AI agents that run continuously in the background and bring in a person only when judgment is needed, a "headless" approach with an agent platform that lets outside developers and AI tools build on its software without its own screens, and a talent-acquisition agent now in early access. Building on the conference news in our 14 Oct edition (Sana as Workday's new home screen and the purchase of ConductorOne, also called C1.ai), these are the new details; Joel Hellermark, Workday's chief AI officer, says people stay in the loop for decisions such as hiring, but the benefit claims are Workday's own.
notes: Enterprise Times page (the pool item) blocked by Cloudflare; read iTWire (Alex Zaharov-Reutt, 16 Oct 2026, who attended as Workday's guest) and InformationWeek (16 Oct 2026) instead. Keynote was 13 Oct 2026 per iTWire. The 14 Oct edition carried SiliconANGLE's report on Sana as the new Workday Home and the purchase of ConductorOne, also called C1.ai.
